question: Which of the following elements is classified as an actinoid group element?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Thorium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Thorium (Th)** is a chemical element with atomic number 90 and is part of the actinoid series, which includes elements 89 to 103.
 
• Actinoids, including thorium, are found in the f-block of the periodic table and are known for their radioactive properties.
 
• Thorium is a naturally occurring, slightly radioactive metal and is primarily used as a nuclear fuel in thorium reactors.
 
• Among the actinoids, thorium is one of the most abundant and has potential applications in advanced nuclear energy systems.
 
• Thorium is distinct from lanthanides like ytterbium, lanthanum, and cerium, which belong to the f-block but are part of the lanthanoid series.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Actinoid Series:**

 
 
• The actinoid series consists of 15 elements ranging from actinium (Ac) to lawrencium (Lr).
 
• These elements are characterized by the filling of the 5f subshell in their electron configurations.
 
• All actinoids are radioactive, with some like thorium and uranium occurring naturally, while others are synthetic.
 
 
 
• **Thorium Applications:**
 
 
• Thorium is used in molten salt reactors and as a fertile material in nuclear energy production.
 
• Its abundance and low waste production make it a promising alternative to uranium in sustainable nuclear energy.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Lanthanoids and Actinoids:**
 
 
• Lanthanoids (elements 57–71) are less radioactive compared to actinoids.
 
• Actinoids have a greater tendency to form complexes and exhibit variable oxidation states.
 
 
 
• **Ytterbium, Lanthanum, and Cerium:**
 
 
• These elements belong to the lanthanoid series, not the actinoid series.
 
• Lanthanoids are known for their magnetic and luminescent properties and are widely used in electronic devices and catalysts.
